title: Mostly bad
body:
EDIT 6/18/25: Checked back in with this app to see if any issues had been addressed; unfortunately I can only add insane lag to the list. When I check off a task, the app seizes up trying to mark it complete. I have invested too much time and money into this app. I’m done!

EDIT 2: Possible scam? I paid for a growth bundle and it only applied to one app instead of the whole bundle. In-app links for support/feedback are all broken. Nice. If you want to complain or request a refund, try going through Apple. Developer does not want to be contacted for some reason.

EDIT: Downgrading my review, because the things I mentioned were actually facets of the same issue. Since I got the app weeks ago, there have been countless unannounced design/format changes. Every time I add a new task, the creation process is somewhat different (ie, you used to be able to add tasks to custom groups; suddenly all my custom groups are gone and tasks can be sorted only by time of day). It’s confusing and makes me wonder if I paid money for a product that was incomplete.

I really like this app. It works with my ADHD. The app generally works fine, and it’s nice to look at. But, two things I don’t get. First, the color palette where I choose the background for my tasks changed today without warning. My old tasks still appear in the old colors, but I can’t make a new task in the old colors, only in a new, muted palette. So being who I am (and someone who relies on color coding), I have to go through and change alllllllll the tasks so they match again. Sigh…okay. Also, the ability to make a monthly task seems to have vanished. I made a monthly task when I first got the app, so I know it was an option before. Why? This is so basic.

title: Hopeful for a response
body:
UPDATED ON APRIL 17, 2025: I think I’m adding a review (and increasing to 3 stars) because I remain optimistic. I’m optimistic that there is some way to get through to customer support. I’m optimistic that the “new management” will fix its mistakes & bugs (most seem to have been addressed), respond to customer feedback without resorting to leaving a review, will bring back shortcut integration, and will honor early adopter life-time upgrade purchases.  So far, one of these things seems to have come true. Please reply to this review or to my emails to you. I will gladly change my rating,and write a superseding review extolling the virtues of this app with so much potential.  It can be one of the best apps of its genre if only …

Sigh.

(If no reply by May, I will concede defeat.  I will do my best to advocate for other early adopters in my shoes, I will sound the alarm so others are not taken in, and I will disappear. Poof! And leave only my legacy.)

UPDATED ON MARCH 5, 2024: No. Don’t download. Previously, an excellent app. (Constructive idea for dev. at end of review.*) Please consider upvoting review so developers will see it.

Original creator bought out a few years ago. After subsequent updates, app remains buggy, features gone. No support response after 6 professional & polite inquiries during 2022. Many better alternatives exist. Truly sad to see it go.  Before the new management, it was one of my favorite apps - that’s the reason for regularly updating my review.  While I will “check-in” occoassiinally, this is the final review (and bit of energy) I will devote to (hopefully) saving this app.

*******************

* = It appears that the developers read the review feedback even if they don’t respond to user queries through their recommended email address/website. Therefore, the following is intended as constructive criticism for developers/owners:

(1) Please honor the few remaining users who paid the full price before change in management. Honoring previous commitments (even if from previous developer) is a common and fair practice.

(1A.) This can be implemented by adding a working “restore purchase” button.

(2) Establish consistent pricing for annual and/or lifetime premium access for those who have started using app since management change.

(3) Focus on development of this app. It still has loads of potential.

title: Finally a simple habits app
body:
I had to write a review on this—I’ve downloaded all the habit tracking apps and can confidently say this is the best one. It’s simple, beautiful, and gives you the features you need to build habits without the unnecessary fluff. 

This company clearly cares a lot about UI/UX and it shows in the incredible design. I’m happy to be a paying subscriber, as this app has allowed new habits to consistently stick for me when other habit trackers have failed me. 

My only suggestions for minor improvements is that sometimes when I edit a habit, it places it out of order of where it was previously. 
Also, I love how clean it is, so if you want to keep the aesthetic simpler I understand, but something that motivates me alongside the Streak is the % of days in which I’ve completed the habit. It’s motivating for me to keep that above 90%, even if my streak had to be reset, so I’d love to see that displayed in subtle, smaller text below the Streak count. 

Thank you for creating this, it’s been amazing!

title: Premium taken away (and then got it back!)

It does indeed seem to be a glitch and I sincerely hope everyone else affected is able to get their accounts fixed. 
With that said, since it was relatively painless to get it fixed and because I do genuinely like the app, I’m updating my review to 5 stars. The simplicity of it is exactly why I like it - the clean look and straightforward tracking without any additional bulk is exactly why I like it enough to have gotten premium in the first place. A lot of habit tracking apps have (in my opinion) unnecessary extra features, but this one is just a very pleasant, clean, straightforward way to keep track of your streaks, which is exactly what I needed.

body:

I hesitated purchasing the premium lifetime for $19.99 based on all of the one star recent reviews. I am unsure what is causing the subscription problem for these users and the lack of tech-support involved is disheartening however, wanted to add a review stating I was successful at purchasing and using a lifetime premium upgrade. 

As someone who has published an app on the Apple App Store, this series of one star reviews may permanently damage the future of this app. So far, I am very happy with this habit tracker so I hope things get worked out. 

The developer should update this apps store description to address the recent slew of subscription problems.

title: Potential Hindered by Technical Glitches, time zones
body:
I've been loyal to Done for over four years, finding benefit in its positive habit tracking features. However, its performance leaves much to be desired. Clicking to mark a task as done often results in a delay of several seconds / minutes or fails to register altogether. With streaks exceeding 1500 days, it's unacceptable that such basic functionality is lacking.

Secondly all the streaks change when you travel across time zones.  It seems to log the time you entered the action, and  if thats in the evening it moves it to the next day when you travel east. 

Despite reaching out to support multiple times, my concerns remain unaddressed.

 I'd gladly award 5 stars if these performance issues were resolved, but until then, I probably seeking and would recommend an alternative app.

title: Best Functioning Habit Tracker App
body:
This is by far the best habit tracker app out there. I am extremely picky and have tried out 40+ habit tracker apps on the appstore (yes, that many). I had very specific needs:

1) non-cluttered
2) monthly view easy to access
3) haptic feedback and sound
4) progress bar instead of a fraction
5) pretty UI
6) notifications
7) weekly view
8) big beautiful icons which is great for adhd
9) ability to have groups
10) easy to navigate

While it is a little spendy, it met all of my needs and have not had any issues whatsoever.

title: Sadly disappointed
body:
I’m so disappointed to have to write a bad review for this app. Up til now it has a great way for me to track and encourage habits, and I like that the interface is clean and simple. 

Because I’ve found the free version of the app both useful and appealing in its simplicity, I decided to pay for the new years special which advertised a lifetime subscription to the paid version of the app for $19.99. I hit purchase. My phone dinged and confirmed the purchase. 

I then clicked through a screen welcoming me… only to discover that none of the upgraded features were available. I WAS charged to my Apple account, and when I tried subscribing AGAIN, just to see if that would do anything, it said I was already subscribed. 

I’ve reloaded the app and restarted my phone several times. And still all I get is the endless frustrating pop up ads advertising the deal I PAID FOR ALREADY. Once I x out of these irritating ads, the app is just the same free version, with no options to add more habits than I already have, which is one of the main reasons I upgraded.

To add a final layer of frustration, I have reached out to the “help” account multiple times and received no emails back. It’s been over a week.

I’m so disappointed that this app, which I was ready to pay more for because I thought it was genuinely worth it, is in fact run by a seemingly unresponsive team who advertise false sales.

-Swipe to change date in the data entry screen was a key feature that was removed. Data entry is not always done on the day it occurred. Having to click on and then navigate the calendar is slow. 

-current day should be indicated in the trended view (when at daily granularity). Helpful when trying to remember whether you entered todays workout or not. 

Thank you for your consideration. And thanks for making an app that has really helped me.

title: Great app to complete daily tasks
body:
Update: still using the app and appreciate all the new features (although the one I requested hasn’t been added as far as I can tell). I’ve recently connected this app with Apple Health to count my daily steps, but the number that is shown in Done is almost always NOT what Apple Health shows. For example, today Apple Health said I walked 6,000 steps, and the Done app said I walked 12,000. 

I really love the app - it’s helped me to stay focused and motivated to complete daily tasks, and I’ll continue to use it. Feature request: the red badge number on the app icon can represent the number of tasks across all habits, not just the number of habits. For example, I have a habit to work on my language studies twice a day. When I mark that I studied in the morning, the red badge number reduces by one because I’ve made progress on the habit, even though I still have another task associated with that habit later on that day. When I look at the red badge number, I want it to represent the number of tasks I have for the day, not the number of habits I have. Otherwise, it seems my only option is to create two separate habits to represent language learning when I want to do that twice per day, but that disrupts the great data visualization, at least in the way that I would like to view them. Perhaps there is a way to adjust the red badge number to represent tasks instead of habits, but if there is, it’s unclear how to do so in the app. Otherwise, thank you for a great app and I’m looking forward to continuing to build my habits.

title: Could use some improvement
body: I appreciate the simple design, the colors, the interface, and the vibration when a habit is complete. The premium is great but doesn’t come with that many more perks. Some improvements or features that can be added to the next update are: - a quick jump between today, yesterday, tomorrow. (instead of clicking on the calendar then day). Like a line with the days of the week over the “all day/ morning/ afternoon/evening”. - being able to select which day weekly habits repeat (you can’t do this now, it will automatically repeat on the day you created the habit). - not asking you every time if you’re sure you want to undo adding a tally to a habit - add monthly habit option - update emoji selection - summary % of how many habits completed overall per day -summary chart has one overall chart for all habits so you can follow trends. - more color options. - health app sync improvements (glitch doesn’t correctly track the number of steps). - being able to include times or timers for habits - having a habit archive: here you can dump a list of habits you want to work on and will add in time. - more appearance features. - adding an option of timeline for when you want to complete the habits each day. This app is great but an update is necessary. I would be disappointed if there isn’t one coming soon.

title: I LOVE this app.
body: As someone with ADHD, this app is an incredibly useful tool for me. I use it to track hours of sleep I get each night (the goal being eight), brushing my teeth and doing skin care twice a day, working out five days a week, walking my dog each day, clean the litter box once a week, etc. In school, I used it to log daily study hours. The only critique I have, is that I found the monthly goals very useful. I’d use that to help me remember chores like deep cleaning the kitchen (you know, like the inside of the oven and microwave that you don’t hit regularly but should do once a month) and taking my dog to the groomers. I’m sad that I can’t add any more of those monthly goals, and my only options are daily and weekly now. Overall, I don’t ever see myself deleting this app. I use it daily and I highly recommend it for anyone who’s ever been called “scatterbrained.”

body:

In the interim they seem to have changed the levels of subscription and only 3 items can be tracked without purchasing premium. There is a recurring special offer that pops up for a lifetime premium membership for $19.99. I looked around at some other similar apps and this seemed to be a great deal.
Except 24 hours later, after the charge has appeared in my card, and after I have received an email receipt from Apple, I am still in basic mode, still with only 3 trackable actions, and still getting the pop-up offer for a lifetime premium membership.
An app that is meant for tracking good habits should have creators who can figure out how to make the special offer actually work.
I will be deleting this and registering complaints with Apple and Amex.
Thanks but no thanks.

title: Free version unusable due to annoying popup
body:
Every time you open up the app when you don’t have the expensive premium plan it nags you with a full screen “limited time offer”. Given that the average workflow is to open the app, quickly mark off a completed habit, and close the app this popup is completely unacceptable and anti user. 

It doesn’t matter what features you have, or how well the app is designed, or how stable it is. You have such an anti user business model that no one should use this app until it is fixed.

Finally, let’s be real, this is a habit tracker, not a streaming service. It’s entire purpose is to provide essentially a daily or weekly checklist. In what world are your per user costs recurring month to month?? A subscription model is inappropriate here and is nothing more than a developer milking you for money because they can. I get that every app does it because it’s somehow acceptable to pay over and over again for the same product nowadays but when combined with the aggressive dark patterns this app uses it feels just so disrespectful. 

No thanks.

body:

PLEASE PRIORITIZE BASIC FUNCTIONALITY:
If your week start day is not Sunday, toggling between the “Habit List” view and the “Graph View” changes the week start date, causing the “Streak” functionally - a critical component to successful habit building - to break. 

This bug has persisted for months, through multiple updates. The latest update just made problem worse by removing the workaround of using the “Date Selector” to re-select “Today”. 

This app is worth the subscription when it works. Please fix this bug and I will immediately update this review to 5-stars.

title: Used to be AMAZING
body:
Notice that all of the rave reviews are from 1-4 years ago. I’ve used this app for 3 or 4 years—a LONG time. It’s a huge part of my day, it’s how I remember to drink enough water, workout, stretch, take my supplements. It also has great stats and charts to track how many times you’ve reached your goals throughout. It’s fun to know my water intake for an entire year, and to compare stats from year to year.
Unfortunately, in the last six months, each thing I love has slowly dropped off, one by one. I lose stats consistently, stats I’ve been collecting for years. It crashes. And now every time I track something, it automatically doubles or triples and I have to go in and ‘undo’. 
I’ve attempted to reach someone many times, with absolutely no answer. It’s like they’ve given up and abandoned the app. Really disappointed I’ve recommend it a ton and loved it for a long time. I now have no choice but to find another app to use. :(

title: Great, but needs work.
body:
First off, I want to get this out of the way and say that the app is effective for getting my you back on track with habits or for starting new habits. However, there are a few issues IMO.

First off, the most important feature of the app is locked behind a paywall. You’re limited to 3 habits to track until you’re required to pay a monthly subscription, which is quite ridiculous for a system that can be replicated with free apps like Notion.

Secondly, the app seems to have a perpetual red notification badge that I cannot manage to make go away, and it is extremely annoying. There is no place in the app to clear or check notifications, and none of these notifications are located in the notification center.

I’m a fan of the app, but there’s just some issues that need to be pointed out before it can truly be great.

title: Excellent Before Update - Removed Features
body:
I used this app with much success to create and track habits. Not just daily or weekly habits, but longer term goals that would span across a month or year. This was incredibly helpful to see progress on goals both on a micro and macro level. 

Sure, I may want a daily goal for drinking a certain number of cups of water, or a weekly goal to get a number of workouts in per week. But what if I want to track a goal to contribute to a charity some number of times a year, or to try a new local restaurant some number of times a month? The previous version of the app allowed me to do this, and it was a major part of the reason I stuck with it and recommended it to others.

If the developer restores this functionality, I would revisit this review. I haven’t heard back from their support team having asked a few times now about this issue over the last few months.

title: Not a huge fan of the design overhaul
body:
Granted, these may just be temporary bugs, or maybe I haven’t dug deep enough through the settings, but I feel like the redesign changed things for the worse. I do like the new aesthetics though, if they just bring back some of these features or fix some of these issues I’d be all on board. 

1) My main issue is: they no longer show you streaks on the dashboard! You can only see streaks if you click into a habit, which I really don’t like. Originally you’d be able to see streaks on the right side of each habit on the dashboard, meaning at a glance you could always see how well you were doing overall. Now you can only see progress for the day or week. No idea they just straight up removed useful info. Even a setting to toggle whether or not to show it would be useful. 

2) They added a calendar icon to more easily go to a specific date, but in the process removed the ability to just swipe to go back and forth a single day. So before, if I wanted to see my list of habits from yesterday, I would just swipe, but now I have to click the calendar, then click yesterday’s date, then click a check mark. Way too many clicks. 

3) This is hopefully just a bug, but some habits no longer show the color bar when you complete them. For me, specifically, this is for Quitting-style habits. It’s still tracking the streaks for me when I complete them, but completing it for the day doesn’t change the color to the one you chose for the habit, it just remains the same color. 

Overall, while I like the aesthetics of the redesign, the utility of the main daily habits dashboard REALLY decreased with this update. Pretty disappointed.

title: Needs improvement
body:
So the app is good for basic daily habit tracking. Set a goal and track it. 

But there’s also a series of annoying oversights. 

First, it doesn’t treat the day a habit to be tracked as the first day for that habit when there’s no prior data (like steps) to track it, so it’s unclear how good or bad you’ve been over time.  Also, streaks aren’t everything, as success percentages matter, as what if a person kept their habit 25/30 days that month? That’s not a way to track it as far as I can tell. 

Second, the app has filters for monthly and yearly goals, but no way to create them.  Adding that would be very useful. 

Third, and this is by far the biggest negative to this app: if you set a goal to do something three times, build that habit and after a week up that target to four times, you lose your streak, because everything pass and present is now judged by that threshold of four times instead of it being from that moment forward.  This is a massive oversight that needs fixing.

title: It’s actually kind of funny how crazy this is!
body: I downloaded after seeing an ad on tiktok and it looked very helpful but it’s definitely not!! My biggest reason being it only allows you to have 3 habits before you have to PAY THEM for making a CHECK LIST lmaoo! First, I wanna get this out of the way, the tiktok ad… false advertising! Nowhere did I see that on the video! The only thing that could be argued as a “warning” would be where it says there’s in app purchases but that could be anything. A majority of apps I see with that and are similar to this one (aka self help apps), the in app purchases are extra bonus features. An example is on an app I have to do a daily check in, one of the extras are videos teaching you about mental health such as anxiety or stress. That makes sense why it would cost extra. The main function/feature of the app doesn’t cost anything unlike this app! This leads me to my next point… I believe this app is a scam! Honestly, who would benefit from having only 3 habits on their list?? At that point it’d be easier and cheaper just to write the list down either as a check list or even a sign in your room or something!

title: What gives with the downgraded widget?
body:
I’ve been using Done since May 2020 and while I love it as a habit tracker, the old widget is what kept me consistent. It seems like not too long after iOS introduced embedded widgets on home pages, the new widget has become useless; I kept waiting to see if an upgrade would bring the old one back, but nope. It used to only be available on the far left widget page, which I didn’t mind scrolling to bc it was visually and functionally just like the actual app. I used to be able to expand the widget to see all 15 of my habits/chores and I could press the number on the far right to log that habit as done - just as you would on the app. Now, you can only see the progress of either 1 or 4 habits with zero interactive capabilities - clicking on the widget just opens the app. Part of what made tracking with Done so effective for me was how frictionless it was to access bc that far left widget page is also one swipe away from the lock screen. Ever since this change, I don’t use it as nearly as much and rarely find myself in the mood to log my habits retroactively. 

Please bring the old widget back! 🙏🏽🙏🏽

title: An actual life-changing app
body: Like every other millennial recently diagnosed with ADHD, I’ve turned to technology to help manage my brain not working so great. And Done has been an incredible help in establishing a routine: making sure I take my meds, that I eat!, even brush my teeth twice a day, etc. That’s where I started and now I have a whole morning sequence that’s so satisfying to check off. It’s so easy to forget those little daily things that make a big difference in health and that I’m now doing it consistently with Done’s help is so huge. I work in software so I also appreciate that side: The app is beautifully designed, it’s SIMPLE, taps and swipes do what you expect them to do - and when they don’t, they do in the next update. It was absolutely the right choice to split productivity functions in the rest of the Growth bundle into separate apps instead of something all-in-one, and while I use and love Last too, Done is as critical as GCal to me at this point. Thank you dev team, seriously - I see the choices you’re making and they are GOOD. I will probably be a lifetime user!

title: overall, great app.
body:
i’ve only recently started using this app. i kept getting adverts for it on instagram and tiktok, and finally decided to download it. i have had similar apps like it, including the same company’s “reflectly” and a similar one, notion. 
i wanted to track the things i do every day and actually get motivation from doing it. i like that you can use numbers to help you, for example, when i drink 1 glass of water, it tells me i have 5 left. which for me personally, is very motivating! 
speaking of motivation, i really like that you can set up your own reminders and notifications for each task. really helpful to someone who never gets things done but eagerly wants to. 

the only reason i rated the app “DONE” as 4 starts instead of 5, is because i wish you wouldn’t have to pay for everything. you can only have 3 tasks, and then you have to pay $9.99 (monthly, if i remember correctly) to have unlimited tasks and any other things that come with the subscription to the app. 

but, overall, i think this is a great app for those who are looking for something to help them get things done, and ACTUALLY do them! 

(and this is coming from someone who never finishes things…until now!).

- lily

author: A LA KAREN

title: Tremendously effective
body:
So you get 5 stars for Done.  The bundle is pretty generic versions of better apps and decidedly redundant, but first year value is excellent. Would I pay $99/yr after that… um no.  But you have a year to change my mind or lower the price. 

I do thoroughly enjoy companies that have a non-legal, plain explanation of privacy. Kudos to you for that. The actual privacy policies freak me out, as they all do.  Not a big fan of other countries having different privacy laws and would appreciate a list of those countries and links to their privacy laws. Not that I would read them, but it’s like diving off a spring board and hoping each country has an actually minimum required water depth. Big fan of not landing on concrete. 

But again, 5 stars for Done. One suggestion, there has to be a workaround for zero goal.  Not all goals are expressed as you numerically envision.  Make it an option in settings please.

title: Great idea, Not worth the price.
body:
This app has the potential to be absolutely fantastic. The free version allows for only 3 goals that you can track with many ways to customize them. It’s cool.

HOWEVER

The app basically begs you to buy the subscription, prompting almost every time you add a data point for a goal. There is no way I’ve found to turn this off. And they’re asking for 60 dollars a year. 60 a year!! Subscriptions are getting wayyy out of hand; there is absolutely no way this app is worth that much. I would happily shell out a one time 5 dollar charge to buy the app, but it is not worth an annual subscription in any way shape or form. 

This app is not worth the download. A hanging whiteboard would be cheaper and more effective.

title: AMAZING for the ADHD brain!
body:
For a person with ADHD, basically every other productivity / habit tracking app out there overcomplicates the work of setting up your habits AND tracking them. 

I want good habits, I don’t need a million bells and whistles and charts. In fact, for most of us with ADHD those are the fastest ways to get hyper focused, distracted, and then bored / quit. 

This app is BEAUTIFUL and simple to use - from the lovely little icon on my Home Screen to the pretty and clean organization of my daily apps. It lets me add a motivation (the “value” behind the goal - which has been shown repeatedly to make the goal more likely to be completed when seen), it clears the items off of my screen when I’ve completed them for the day (that’s one of the view options), it allows me to log a note or entry with my count that is easy to retrieve and see all notes at a glance, and the best part, it allows me to set a reminder for a specific time that only goes off when the goal is unmet!

This app is a lifesaver! My only suggestion, start small - pick 2-3 easily achievable daily goals (rather than weekly): floss your teeth, make your bed in the am, take your vitamins/meds, etc). Once you start feeling proud for checking things off, add no more than 1-2 new goals a week or 1 new weekly goal! GOOD LUCK with your new habits! I’m rooting for you!

title: Great for forming positive habits
body:
If you make yourself care about this, as I have, it’s a great way to hold yourself accountable for the things you want for yourself. I decided this month that I wanted to form positive habits and control some of the chaos in my life. It feels so satisfying to log an activity, not just for the colors and the app, but to look at it and say “I did these things every day” or “I meditated/exercised three times a week.” It really helped me realize how much better you feel when you introduce routine activities into your free time. I got the growth bundle and am slowly introducing myself to the other apps in the package. Aside from Done, Do and Grateful are my favorites. If you have the $10 to drop on the promo, I’d say it’s worth it to at least give them a try. Some are redundant-seeming, but this is a good way to try the premium features on the bundle for a year and see what you’ll want to keep after that. 

Only did the 4 stars because Done will sometimes/often glitch when I open it, returning me to the Home Screen and taking some of the satisfaction out of logging my activity. Other than that I haven’t had any problems.

title: Small suggestion that would drastically help
body:
I love this app so much. It has helped motivate me with so many daily and weekly goals. 

There is one update I hope the developers will one day work on. There is no way to easily track/view your stats on a WEEKLY goal basis. For instance: one of my weekly goals is to do 100 push-ups. When viewing the graph of this bar you can view by WEEK MONTH or YEAR. When viewing the WEEK stat it shows a breakdown of individual days rather than a single number. This should be a separate section labeled DAYS. The WEEK layout should simply show the TOTAL FOR THE WEEK rather than showing how much each day. For example, when I’m trying to see how Many push-ups I did this week vs last week it should just show one single number of the TOTAL of last week and the total of this week. Instead it shows a daily breakdown. 

That would be the one thing that would help users really track their weekly progress with ONE TOTAL number being shown rather than the entire weeks worth of individual daily stats.

title: It’s good, but could use some easy improvements for night shifters
body: I work night shift at a hospital so I typically go to bed around 11am. This causes my daily goals to be reset halfway through my day. They have in the settings an option that lets you change your days start time which helps fix it, but only lets you go as late as 5am. Why limit it to that? Why not allow any time? They let you go back to previous days to fill it in, but it’s annoying to have to go back to the previous day every time you want to add to it. Also if you use their widget to easily update your goal, even if you change the start time to 5am, it clears the goal at midnight. That’s not that bad though because even though it looks like it’s starting over on a new day, if you go in the app it’s still adding it to the correct day in regards to your start time. I like the app but a few simple fixes could make it way better for all night shifters.

title: Lost my data :(
body:
Pros: Simple to use. Let’s you track habits you want to build (Drink more water! Take vitamins!) and those you want to stop (No coffee today!). Love that you can do all that in one app. It takes some practice but is pretty easy to set up your habits. I happily used the app from January to May 2021.

Then, yesterday (May 22), I discovered that it had lost some of my data. For example, I had a “no wine” streak of 109 days going and was very proud of my accomplishment. When I tried to add record another day I saw that all my no wine days had been deleted. Same thing with a few (but not all) of my other habits. So disappointing to lose that history.

I would’ve recommended this to anyone and everyone before yesterday but now I really can’t recommend at all. Super frustrating.

title: Update: formerly great, new owners, now avoid
body:
The good: This app has allowed me to create and stick to habits and goals I never would have thought possible for me. Transformative impact on my life.

The bad: the app - and all those in the growth bundle - have been taken over by a new owner developer and have gotten much worse. The original creator was a wonderful, passionate developer who built truly awesome, helpful products single handedly. I emailed with her a couple of times and she was awesome. 

Recently I noticed significant declines in performance across the app suite. I investigated and found that some new company “Reflectly” is now listed as the creator. These guys

- don’t answer service requests (or when they do they are completely pro forma useless comments)
- extort you on pricing 
- provide useless release notes - look at the version history and you can see when they took over 

It’s a terrible shame because these guys are gutting these wonderful products. It is completely antithetical to the spirit in which they were first created. I don’t know what happened but even if the original developer made a lot of money (I hope she did!) I still imagine her heart is breaking to see how these guys are trashing her creation. And my heart breaks for all us users who have lost some truly life changing tools. RIP.

title: Done with Done
body:
I wish I could do 2 reviews - one for the app, and another for the developer. The app is great - simple, stable, easy to use, motivating. I have used it for over a year and was willing to pay its going rate (a one-time fee). I thought it was worth the low price.

Now the app has gone to a subscription model and the price has skyrocketed. To be fair, the developer has given me a period of time to upgrade to the subscription model at a good discount. But the fact is that this is a pretty simple app that doesn’t get updated very often, and rarely adds new features. Seems to me a subscription should get me a lot more than a bug fix a year and no real new features. And what I liked about Done was that it really needed no new features - it did just what I wanted and the price for that was fair.

I see that almost every similar app costs, so I will have to pay for something. But unless the app gets frequent updates or features, I won’t be paying for anything on a subscription model. Too bad - Done is a great app - but I’m done with Done.

title: The perfect blend of simplicity and customization
body: I’ve used the free version of this app several times, but I ALWAYS end up subscribing.  I’ve tried a million other reminder/habit tracking/wellness apps and I keep coming back to this one.  It is the best app I’ve found that allows the perfect amount of customization without being overwhelming.  The interface is super user friendly, you can set as many habits as you want, you can specify if you want to build or quit the habit (the ONLY app I’ve found that does that!), and even set multiple reminders for a habit.  For example, I have reminders set to drink water every two hours on weekdays but none on weekends bc I don’t want them to wake me up.  My only possible suggestion would be to include even more colors for the habits for people like me who have approximately 1,000,000 habits I need to be held accountable for!
author: Ihatepickingthesethings!

title: Great User Display That Could Do With an Improved User Set
body:
I sought out and downloaded Done entirely for the way it displays the habits. I like the colorful list style display of habits. Easy to see completion of all items and streaks at a glance. 

While it is by no means the power user rival of Streaks, it does have some customization in terms of frequency of tasks regarding number of times per days, week, month, or year. You can also set multiple reminders and create custom units.  No way to do timer based tasks though, you’ll have to track the time outside of the app or guesstimate how long you’ve spent. 

There is a dark mode, but no option to have it switch automatically. Seems like that would be a quality of life no brainer!

There is some Apple Health integration, but only for 10 or so preset tasks. Water is strangely absent. 

Ultimately, I gave it one star higher than Streaks because while it lacks many of the features, I find it easier to scan and use for the most part! That said, for the rather high price of the subscription - $24 a year!!!! - compared to the fairly low flat price of Streaks, one would expect a bit more polish and integration. Like, for the level of where this app is, I would expect it to cost what Streaks does and Streaks to cost what this does!

title: Subscription price is a too much for little return
body:
Yearly subscription for $19.99??? If there was maybe a $10 flat fee to unlock premium permanently then I’d pay. But a yearly subscription is pushing it. You can’t make more than 3 habits without being prompted to upgrade to their subscription. I know it only comes to less than $2 a month but that’s excessive for an app that’s just going to give me daily reminders. If anything I can just program my notes app to do that and it’ll be free. 

There’s no flexibility in your subscription options either, you cannot do a monthly payment to try it out for a few months to see if you vibe with it, you’re just stuck committing for the whole year unless you’re fine with 3 habits a time.

 I’d pass up on this. Track your habits using something else unless you’re willing to pay $20 for the aesthetic.

The app is simple, clean and easy to set up habits and alarms. The font is a bit small but that’s also just a preference. The color coding is a nice touch and helps everything appear organized. Overall this app looks like it would work well and be helpful to a lot of people, myself included. You just really need to look past the yearly subscription for what basically is a notification app. 

I personally don’t recommend it until the app offers more for their current price or they reduce their yearly sub price completely or better yet offer more flexible sub options.

title: Excellent app, questionable pricing
body:
Do NOT subscribe through Done. The prices are more expensive. 

I wanted to buy this app, but it seems like the one-time purchase is no longer an option. I swear it was there a few days ago, and I read a MacRumors app recap from August 23 that mentioned the $8.99 one-time upgrade. In the Apple Store, both Done and the Growth Bundle state that the premium upgrade is available in-app. However, the only options in the app are $20/yr for the standalone app or $30/yr for the bundle. Maybe they changed their pricing scheme and haven’t updated the descriptions. However, pricing isn’t consistent across apps: the others offer the Growth Bundle subscription for $19/yr, which makes the annual subscription for Done more expensive than the entire Growth Bundle. I’m really disappointed because I wanted to support this app, but due to what seems like price gouging, I won’t.

If you must, I’d recommend subscribing through one of their other apps. And if you’d like to purchase one, not subscribe, the four apps besides Done and Tally are reasonably priced at $3 to $5. It would honestly be cheaper to buy those four for life than to subscribe for a year.

The app makes habit tracking easy and effortless. It requires a one time payment of $8.99 (plus tax) in comparison to the other apps that require monthly payments. title: Beautifully and simply design, solid goal tracker
body:
I love this app! I’ve been using this for a few months to help track goals. It’s simple to use, while still having a solid set of features. It allows you to tack both goals you’re building towards (ex. Daily meditation, exercising 4x/week) or trying to quit/reduce (ex. Quit drinking). I paid for the upgrade so I could track more goals after I hit the limit because I was finding it actually helped me keep motivated. (And also to get upgrades on two of their other awesome apps - Grateful and Moody)

My three feature requests (stack ranked)  

1. Goals are sorted alphabetically and you can’t rearrange them. What I want is a way to view all my goals grouped by category. For example, I want to see my physical health goals (exercise 4x/week, eat healthy) grouped and my personal enrichment goals (meditate daily, read daily, journal 2x/week) grouped. It does allow you to tag goals with categories and filter by category, but I don’t find the filtering useful because I want to see all the goals at once. This would give me a birds eye view of how I’m doing in different parts of my life (physical health, mental health, hobbies, etc.). 

2. Integrations with your other apps, Moody and Grateful. For example I want to see a goal to enter my mood three times a day and make an entry in Moody daily. I would like Done to automatically know when I’ve completed those goals in the other apps.

Currently the app has bar charts for your goals. For the types of goals I’m tracking, I don’t find this visualization particularly helpful. For example, if I hurt my daily meditation goal every day for a month it’s just a bunch of equal height bars. I do like the idea of visualizing data on my goals and hope you do more explorations there. 

Overall an awesome app! (If anyone who works there reads this, I signed up for Beta and would be happy to participate in research!)

title: Love it, could be more fully featured
body:
Love this app because you get the satisfaction of seeing the bars rise every time you complete something. Also love that you can set a goal to quit something, which means that I don’t need a separate app to track how many drinks I’ve had in a day, like I needed with it’s competitor, “Productive”. This app also has a much more intuitive interface than Productive.

Things I dislike are that you can’t separate tasks into “time of day” like you could with Productive. This could be accomplished very easily by separating the “today” pane into “anytime” “morning” “afternoon” “evening” and “night”, each of which would appear as long as there were habits/goals assigned to be completed at those times. Only after you swiped backwards past those panes would you be able to get to previous days. And then, after a certain amount of time the app would reset to the pane that matched the time of day it was being viewed, to show you the tasks that needed to be completed within that timeframe.

At any rate this app only gets updated every few months, so I don’t think that’ll happen.

title: My skin is looking great!
body: I’ve always struggled to keep up a solid skincare routine. In the days of skincare-crazed social media, I was feeling the pressure to be better to my skin. Plus, I’d seen my skin shine on the few consistent days I could keep up a good habit. I knew better days were right around the corner, but I needed incentive to make it happen. Here’s where Done comes in. Thanks to Done, I’m on a 15 day streak of healthy hygiene habits, and me and my skin are absolutely glowing. I’m halfway to building a healthy habit, but I don’t think I’ll quit Done once I’m washing my face twice a day every day for the rest of my life. There are plenty of other habits Done can help me build and I’m already setting more goals. I haven’t upgraded to the paid services because I don’t want to over-do it—two (three, actually) habits at a time seem like the perfect amount of responsibility. Thanks to Done, my goals seem a little more achievable. PS, my favorite feature? The ability to add habits completed after midnight to the day before. Don’t wanna break that streak just because I stayed up too late!

author: Isaachou

title: Some Adjustments Needed
body:
I like the simplicity in that this tool is relatively intuitive.  But I have a feeling some good video demo links with someone who knows it better would help me understand how to use the more advanced tools.

The free version is limited to 3 goals, which seems a bit slim so as to make it hardly worth using.

So far (using the paid app) I have not found a way to graph or summarize my progress for multiple goals or habits together overall or by category, or an easy way to weight them by importance.  This would be my most desirable feature.  Graphing is pretty limited and I’ve yet to really find the charts any better than simply looking at overall counts.  As with the charts, the counts should have some way of summarizing so that you can give an overall score summary.  If that exists, I have not yet figured it out on my own.

I like that there are reminders to enter results throughout the day at times of my choosing and that you can choose to “quit” or “add” each habit and the graphic adjusts accordingly.  However, I find that the graphics with some add and some quit behaviors next to each other are really confusing and are not good for understanding progress at a glance.  So after using the app for a few days I’ve modified my goals to all be add behaviors.

At the moment I’ve only been tracking binary goals as for whether I did them or not.  But I can envision that I’ll want to ultimately track calories or running distance such that I’ll get more from my graphs.  

For now what’s going to keep me using this app is that it keeps me accountable to keep feeding data.  But if I find that the output is not showing trending effectively over time I can see it going away for me.

For example: if working out is a goal but the workout consists of pushups, sit-ups, and squats, you can’t partially check off each one. It’s an all or nothing one item click. I also am using it now for some recurring to-do list items and it’s good but each item has to be its own thing instead of parts of a whole. 
Worth buying for straight habit tracking.

title: I really adore this app
body:
Functional, relatively simple, and rewarding to use on a day to day basis. Motivates me, keeps me accountable and organized!

The only reason I can’t give this app five stars right now is it’s really BEGGING for more robust, user-friendly analysis. 

The summary page is frankly useless. It’s impossible to gauge my progress over time with all my habits stratified across different graphs that I can’t view without scrolling down the page and leaving the previous graph behind. A meaningful summary of my data is completely unattainable with this layout. 

There are some great suggestions in previous reviews which I would love to see implemented, but my big two requests are:

1) Show a week-by-week summary of all my habits (or a filtered selection) using the calendar system from the individual habit pages. Take seven days of data from each habit (using the existing calendar notation system) and just stack them on top of each other so that I can see patterns in how I [fail to] achieve my goals. 

2) I would love to see a summary of my streaks for all my habits side by side on the same page. I want to see:

1. longest streak
2. current streak
3. number of times I’ve performed a habit during my current streak

for each habit. As a side note, the “goals met” metric is not particularly useful to me, as it includes old data that I no longer find relevant. It would be nice to have the option to replace it with something like my above suggestion. 

Thanks so much for a useful and beautiful app - and please, please please consider making some changes to the analysis tools!

title: Really Great!  No subscription, worth the $$, one suggestion.
body:
I tried several apps to help me develop better habits and regiment, and this was the best.  

The colors and sounds are a nice effect (though there are two reddish colors that are almost exactly the same... :P Haha)

Most calendar, productivity, to-do, or habit apps require a subscription after the trial.  This app does not, which is a huge selling point.  While I get the subscription business model, for those of us who don’t have money to spare but still need help being more productive, a one-time charge is preferable. And it’s not just about the money.  With a subscription I’m continually paying for my ability to be productive, I’m getting “hooked on a drug” then being repeatedly charged for its use.  A one-time charge is a lot less exploitative, and doesn’t come with the same guilt (which we don’t need when fixing our habits).

*** My one caveat.  Could the reminders have the same timing options as the habits themselves?  I have a habit that I only do on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.  But I can’t set a reminder for those days.  The closest thing is weekdays.

title: A few suggestions
body:
First off, I love this app! However I have a few suggestions. 

First in setting where you can sort you habits (last, first, manual etc) please add "group" so I can simply move things around by groups. I'm aware I can view by group at the top. 

Second allow change of the font/habits size. I have a lot of habits, I'd like not to scroll forever and viewing more at once is motivating. 
*Another idea/take on this. Perhaps also have a button or page called or with icon expressing "view all habits" this page would simply show all your habits in a much smaller font in their color. This provides an easy quick view of what habits we already have for of us in a visually helpful form. Similar to how they are shown when you go to manual ordering and then press set. 

Under the charts page please add a feature where you can view all your habits on one chart (let's say the bottom) with the amount of times you did them (on the left) and be able to change the time frame of the viewing (days, weeks etc)
While I'm thinking on this one might add the problem is that this doesn't really display how man times you hit your goal just the amount of times you did it. Perhaps the ones where you hit your goal will be in their color while ones yet complete are in gray similar to the front screen. 

I'll add more as I think of it.

title: What I was looking for
body:
Pros 
Good for building and quitting  habits
Makes user input data daily
Reminders
Customizable 
Tracks data
Free version shows enough to get a feel for the app
User friendly

Cons
Has to be used daily ( which isn't really a con)
Calender visuals for all habits would be helpful too

I needed a habit tracker to hold myself accountable for building good habits and minimizing bad habits. 

The app gives lots of options like reminders and notifications. It doesn't allow me to go back and add data if I forgot to input it that day but that just aids in accountability. 

After trying out the features I upgraded to the paid version and it was well worth it. Gives more access and options. You can have more than three habits with the paid version, as well as set multiple reminders.

There are charts to track activity. It shows week month and yearly data in a chart and calendar. The calendar visuals only shows one habit at a time. It would be nice to have a calendar visual on the main page where the charts are that allows users to see progress customized in a calendar.

I really like this app.

title: Love it!
body:
Don’t hesitate to give this a try....  This app is cleanly designed, nice to look at, and reasonably priced.  I didn’t hesitate to upgrade after playing with the free version (limited to 3 goals) for a few hours.  

It is easy to use (though navigation takes a bit to figure out), has good instructions, within the app, and looks great!  There is also a Share icon at the bottom, and I was pleased to see a number of integrations, including Trello which I use daily. (I can send a success note to one of my boards!)  I also like the Journal feature. Great to be able to jot yourself a note to help track your progress.... deepens the ‘streak’ narrative.

I had been playing with another app which limited to 3 tasks (without making that clear at the front end, then required me to sign up for a free trial... 7 days, then $23.99 annual subscription fee... really?).  SO glad to find this app as an alternative!  Enjoy!

title: I LOVE This App- From a Mom.
body: I use this a little differently than most probably do. I have lots of little kids and am frequently an overstimulated and overwhelmed mom. I realized that the only time I was intentionally touching my kids was when I hugged them at night, that I was nagging them all the time, and not spending individual time with them. I’ve read that for kids to emotionally thrive they have to be touched a certain amount of times per day. I set a goal for each of them to touch them, compliment them, and spend time with them every day. This has been so nice to see which kids need the attention because I can see who has been missed. It helps me to focus and remember through the day. And the amazing thing is, the more I focus on them, the happier and less overwhelmed I am. Funny how that works. 😉The only thing missing is a widget!

title: Life was clutter, Now it’s all getting DONE!
body:
I was disorganized, stressed out and putting off things that really mattered to me.  I got tired of it.  And it just all wasn’t working.  I needed structure and goals in my life!

Enter the “DONE” app.  
I was committed and willing to change.  I tried a few apps then discovered DONE.  It was refreshingly simple which attracted me to engage with it.  Once I logged a good chunk of my activity, I could see it was complex enough to use as a lifestyle management tool.  And so I went with it.  

And now, haven spent much time with the DONE app, I actually feel more satisfied, EVEN HAPPIER because I now have wrapped my head around what was once the chaotic assortment of things cluttering my life.  This app helps me bring order to the chaos — thus making life run smoother, more effective.  Now I’ve found myself in a place I didn’t expect — when I have a handle on the stressors and work load of my daily life, I am effective and focused enough to really dig in and work on my long-term aspirations!

*** One thing I’d like to see this app incorporate is a more personalized, customizable overall theme.  I’m a visual person and find I spend much time with the app so I’d like to make it my own.  To be able to use my pictures in the background of a trend chart, or as an icon for given goal categories.  A picture of what and who is important to me would help me keep my eye on the prize.  I could also see the app yielding a more personal touch by providing a choice of fonts, maybe changeable upon each category to more effectively display the different aspects of my life.  

Thanks so much!

title: Beautiful AND functional
body: I have tried the following “habit” apps: Habit-Bull, Productivity, Way of Life! and Daily Goals. In some, I even upgraded to paid features. In each case, I sighed, “Why does creating habits have to be so d’mn ugly?” With Habit-Bull, I expected some roided-out CrossFit guy to jump out of the app and scream, “Drop and give me 20!” I gave up and then spent way too much money, trying to make a Bullet Journal look like the ones on Pinterest. (Seriously, who has that time?) After throwing away, my last attempt at paper habit tracking, I came back to the App Store and found a friendly app called “Tally”. It did the job, simply keeping track of my successful days. After some success, I found myself wanting the “streak” feature. So, I went back to the App Store. I downloaded Habit-Bull again and didn’t make it past the login screen before that roided-out guy was screaming at me. Productivity? “Why do we have to be so dark about things?” I didn’t even download the latter two again. Then I saw done in the App Store, as if it were winking at me and saying, “We got this.” I downloaded it and fell in love. If there is one word to describe this app, it’s friendly. The classical music sounds (that can be muted) are fun rather than stodgy. The interface is clean and bright. This is *the app* if you’re looking for medium-level data on habit tracking and a beautiful, friendly interface. Thanks, guys! Keep up the good work! p.s. I would love to see what you would come up with if did a planner/to-do app.

author: Lunar Dount

title: This App is 100% Worth The Long Review
body: I’ve tried several different habit tracker apps to monitor and increase/decrease the frequency of several activities in my life, but none of them come close to Done. A lot of these apps can have too many features, which I find gets in the way of successfully altering a habit. Done is simple, attractive and easy to use, while still providing a more than detailed breakdown of your habit statistics. When I found that I wanted to track a few smaller aspects of a certain habit, I discovered the journal feature. The journal feature was one of my favorite parts because it allowed me to write down the information and details about a specific day. For instance, if I’m trying to reduce how often I go on Instagram, when updating my progress I can make a note of maybe how long I spent on insta each time that I opened it. This feature allowed me to add a more personal touch to my goals, which definitely made them easier to keep up with, and just a little more rewarding when I achieved them. On top of all that, the app is absolutely gorgeous. You can assign a color to each goal, all of which are vibrant and pleasing. The app has a sleek, minimal interface that’s attractive but not distracting or confusing. I would 100% recommend the Done app for any goals or habit tracking needs you have. I’ll definitely be buying the unlimited version very soon!

title: Good Enough.
body:
The app does exactly what it’s meant to and is worth the couple dollars to upgrade for unlimited tasks. It’s easy, consistent, bug-/glitch-free (in my experience), and can even be exported as an Excel .csv file. 

I’ve noticed a couple areas of improvement as well:

1. One task = one reminder. So if I want to drink eight classes of water a day, I either create eight tasks with a reminder at a different time OR I set one task to drink water with a goal of eight and remind myself using another app. 
   There should be an option to set multiple reminders or alarms per task. 

2. You can’t set goals for certain times (not referring to reminders). Assume I were on some special diet plan that tells me I need to remove sugar on week one, grains on week two, dairy on week three, etc. The app will let me create a task that says something like “no sugar/grains/dairy”, but it won’t let me limit the “no sugar” task to a week—it’ll just stay there forever until I delete the task; nor will it let me to create the “no dairy” task to a certain time in the month (e.g. three weeks from today). 
   There should be an option to assign tasks to days in a week/month/etc., while also allowing for an end goal date.
